summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and prostate cancer on radiation therapy, was admitted after a pre-syncopal episode at his oncology appointment. He presented with signs of sepsis secondary to a Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary tract infection that had spread to the bloodstream. His condition was complicated by urinary obstruction from prostate cancer, leading to hydronephrosis in both native and transplanted kidneys. A Foley catheter was placed to relieve retention, and he was started on cefepime, later broadened to meropenem before reverting to cefepime based on sensitivities. He had ongoing treatment for C. difficile with oral vancomycin, which was continued. A PICC line was placed for outpatient IV antibiotics. His kidney function improved, and he was discharged home with plans to complete a 14-day course of cefepime, continue oral vancomycin for two weeks post-antibiotics, and follow up with urology. His rosuvastatin was held due to elevated liver enzymes, and omeprazole was switched to pantoprazole to avoid interaction with clopidogrel.
